paper_metadata.title: Prognosis of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy 45 years after onset: Seizure outcome and predictors

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the inclusion criteria and baseline characteristics. However, the sample is a convenience cohort from a single specialized center, and the authors explicitly acknowledge a potential selection bias toward highly motivated, compliant patients with higher socioeconomic backgrounds, which may not represent the general JME population.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The records of the 339 patients with IGE showed that 82 patients had been diagnosed with JME; 190 had absence epilepsy, 51 had GTCS on awakening, and 16 had unclassifiable generalized epilepsy.
items.reasoning: The authors describe the source population (IGE patients at Charité–Universitätsmedizin Berlin) and the specific subset diagnosed with JME.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Many of our patients made a special effort to see a specialized epileptologist, which implies high motivation and probably a higher educational and socioeconomic background.
items.reasoning: While the recruitment from hospital records is clear, the authors admit the sample is likely biased toward a specific socioeconomic and motivated demographic.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: last patient contact (personally or via telephone interview between January and July 2011).
items.reasoning: The final contact period is clearly defined, and the retrospective nature implies recruitment spanned the decades of the senior author's practice.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location) are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: treated at the Department of Neurology, Charité–Universitätsmedizin Berlin
items.reasoning: The specific clinical setting and institution are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We included patients who had been diagnosed with JME according to the classification of the International League Against Epilepsy (1989) and had been followed up for at least 20 years.
items.reasoning: Standard ILAE criteria and a specific follow-up duration were used for inclusion.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Of 82 patients with a diagnosis of JME, sufficient information on seizure outcome was available for 66 patients... indicating a recruitment rate of more than 80%.
items.reasoning: A participation rate of >80% is generally considered low risk for selection bias within the identified cohort.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Clinical data for all patients included in the study are presented in table 1.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides age at onset, sex, EEG findings, and presence of absence seizures.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for the 16 excluded patients and performs a sensitivity analysis comparing them to the included cohort, finding no significant differences in key prognostic variables.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: sufficient information on seizure outcome was available for 66 patients (33 female and 33 male), indicating a recruitment rate of more than 80%.
items.reasoning: The retention of over 80% of the eligible diagnosed cohort is high for a 45-year follow-up study.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Sixteen patients who were excluded from the study did not differ significantly from the final study population regarding age at epilepsy onset and at investigation, sex, and occurrence of absence seizures
items.reasoning: The authors attempted to compare the dropouts/excluded patients with the study group to assess bias.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 16 of 82 patients... did not meet the inclusion criteria, 8 because of insufficient documentation of data and another 8 because of loss to follow-up.
items.reasoning: Specific reasons for exclusion/attrition are provided.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Sixteen patients who were excluded... did not differ significantly... regarding age at epilepsy onset and at investigation, sex, and occurrence of absence seizures
items.reasoning: The authors explicitly state they checked for differences in key prognostic factors between those lost and those analyzed.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: Sixteen patients who were excluded from the study did not differ significantly from the final study population
items.reasoning: Statistical comparison confirmed no significant differences in baseline characteristics.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors were derived from clinical records and standardized EEG, managed by a single expert, ensuring consistency in measurement across the cohort.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Potential predictors of seizure outcome assessed in this study were age at onset of JME, genetic traits (epilepsy in first-degree relatives), first interictal EEG... appearance of absence seizures, sex, and insurance status
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly listed and defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All included patients were diagnosed and treated by the same doctor, a senior epileptologist and one of the authors (D.J.).
items.reasoning: Consistency is high due to a single expert performing the assessments, though it relies on retrospective record review.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Age at onset, y, mean 6 SD 14.3 6 4.1
items.reasoning: Continuous variables like age are reported as means/SDs without arbitrary categorization.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All included patients were diagnosed and treated by the same doctor... homogeneous diagnostic criteria and treatment strategies
items.reasoning: The single-center, single-physician design ensures high uniformity in measurement.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: 8 because of insufficient documentation of data... All 66 patients finally included had myoclonic jerks and GTCS
items.reasoning: Patients with missing data were excluded initially, ensuring the analyzed cohort had complete PF data.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study excluded patients with insufficient data rather than using imputation.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) is clearly defined, but for a portion of the cohort, it relies on patient recall via telephone/questionnaire, which is subject to recall bias, especially over such a long follow-up period.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: 5-year terminal remission... defined as the time between onset of JME... and last patient contact
items.reasoning: The primary outcome is clearly defined as 5 years of seizure freedom at the end of the follow-up.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Forty-six patients answered directly by telephone or by returning the questionnaire. The remaining 20 patients were included based on detailed documentation in their case records
items.reasoning: While clinical records are used, the reliance on self-reported seizure freedom via telephone for the majority of patients introduces potential recall bias.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Forty-six patients answered directly by telephone... The remaining 20 patients were included based on detailed documentation in their case records
items.reasoning: There was a split in how outcome data were collected (direct contact vs. record review), though the authors found no demographic differences between these groups.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses univariate analyses to identify predictors. While it identifies absence seizures as a predictor, it does not perform a multivariable adjustment to control for potential confounding between the measured variables (e.g., age of onset and absence seizures).

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Potential predictors... were age at onset of JME, genetic traits... first interictal EEG... appearance of absence seizures, sex, and insurance status
items.reasoning: Key clinical and demographic variables were measured.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1 Summary of clinical data... Table 3 Overview of AED treatment
items.reasoning: Confounders like AED type and EEG patterns are categorized and defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All included patients were diagnosed and treated by the same doctor
items.reasoning: The use of a single expert and clinical records for baseline confounders is relatively reliable.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patient data were analyzed based on the case records
items.reasoning: Baseline confounders were extracted from the same clinical record system.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Imputation was not used; missing data led to exclusion.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study did not use matching or stratification in its design to account for confounding.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: For comparison of patients with 5-year terminal remission and those without, Fisher exact test was used for categorical dependent variables, and univariate analysis of variance was used for metric-dependent variables.
items.reasoning: The analysis relied on univariate tests (Fisher exact, ANOVA). There is no evidence of multivariable logistic regression or Cox proportional hazards modeling to adjust for confounding.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the descriptive and exploratory nature of the study, and the results are reported transparently, including effect sizes.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Data were analyzed using SPSS version 18.0 software... Fisher exact test was used for categorical dependent variables, and univariate analysis of variance was used for metric-dependent variables.
items.reasoning: The statistical approach is clearly described.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Potential predictors of seizure outcome assessed in this study were...
items.reasoning: The variables selected are clinically relevant, but no complex model building (e.g., stepwise selection) was performed as the analysis was univariate.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test revealed that all metric variables were normally distributed... variances were homogeneous
items.reasoning: The authors verified the assumptions for the parametric tests used.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: All clinical variables of seizure outcome are presented in table 2.
items.reasoning: The study reports results for all assessed predictors, including non-significant ones.
